title: The tensor insertion transports scalars through the inverse coefficient map
statement: Fix D,l,E and a point automorphism g as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with no characteristic hypothesis, and an arbitrary strict coefficient module system M on the ringed sequence site [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. For a natural index n and a pro-etale object U, let j_(n,M,U)(x) be the actual finite pullback adjunction-unit generator restricted along the canonical comma arrow [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison, def-pur-integral-finite-pullback], for x in the original module M_n(gU). If c_n:F_n(B_n)->B_n is the canonical coefficient isomorphism, then j_(n,M,U)(c_n(U)^(-1)(a)*x)=a*j_(n,M,U)(x) for every a in B_n(U). The scalar action on x is the original strict-system action, including the evaluation coefficient-ring identification. No normalized-system or transition hypothesis is required.

proof.text: For a generic module-sheaf pushforward through a ring morphism, restriction of scalars gives the source action by applying that ring morphism to the scalar. A morphism from that pushforward is therefore linear for the transported action. Apply this to the normalized ordinary tensor comparison of lem-trf-point-system-finite-tensor-comparison at the evaluated finite module.

proof.text: Evaluation is pushforward on the level slice through an equality cast of coefficient rings. The identity-on-sections normalization of lem-trf-point-system-ordinary-evaluation-comparisons says each component of this ring cast is the identity. Thus its module action is the original system action. Substitute this identity in the preceding linearity equation and use the normalized tensor-unit formula on both sides. This proves the asserted equality for every scalar and section.

theorem tensor_insertion_smul (n : ℕ)
    (M : coefficientSequenceModules l E (Spec (.of D.k)))
    (U : (Spec (.of D.k)).ProEt)
    (a : (integralCoefficientSheaf l E (Spec (.of D.k)) n).obj.obj (op U))
    (x : M.val.obj (op (n, (proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U))) :
    (fun y : M.val.obj (op (n, (proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U)) ↦
      (((integralOperationsLevelPullback.{t, u} l E g n).obj
        ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E (Spec (.of D.k)) n).obj M)).val.map
          (proEtaleIsoCommaArrow g U).op)
          (integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l E g n
            ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E (Spec (.of D.k)) n).obj M)
            ((proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U) y))
        (@HSMul.hSMul _ (M.val.obj (op (n, (proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U)))
          (M.val.obj (op (n, (proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U))) inferInstance
          ((inv (inverseImageFiniteCoefficientMap l E g n)).hom.app (op U) a) x) =
      a • (fun y : M.val.obj (op (n, (proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U)) ↦
      (((integralOperationsLevelPullback.{t, u} l E g n).obj
        ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E (Spec (.of D.k)) n).obj M)).val.map
          (proEtaleIsoCommaArrow g U).op)
          (integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l E g n
            ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E (Spec (.of D.k)) n).obj M)
            ((proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U) y)) x
